Endoscopy: Esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD) revealed normal esophageal mucosa and normal biopsies.
High-resolution manometry (HRM):
  - Revealed absent esophageal peristalsis
  - Median integrated relaxation pressure (IRP) > 15 mm Hg
  - No lower esophageal sphincter (LES) relaxation with swallows
  - Increased intraluminal pressure throughout the esophagus with swallows

bindings.label: Patient is a 22-year-old man; physical examination results were unremarkable

Despite taking omeprazole (20 mg once daily) 30 minutes before breakfast, avoiding foods that precipitated symptoms, and sleeping with head elevated, heartburn and regurgitation while supine continued
He reported intermittent solid-food dysphagia for 2 years with no weight loss (body weight 254 lb [115 kg])
High-resolution manometry shows absent esophageal peristalsis, IRP >15 mmHg, impaired LES relaxation, and increased intraesophageal pressure during swallowing
Upper endoscopy is normal and biopsies are negative
pH-impedance monitoring and barium swallow study were not performed; expert analyses state HRM is diagnostic for achalasia without them
Serum tryptase was elevated at 42 ng/mL and the bone marrow aspirate showed mast cell infiltration
